title: rpt command record
description: One command rpt <name> can run, emitted by rpt help: the built-ins in name order, then the plugins on PATH in name order. Described with the members a --describe answer uses; a plugin's come from its answer, unknown ones included, and are absent when it gave none in time.

name.description: The command, as in rpt <name>; for a plugin, its file name without the rpt- prefix.

path.description: A plugin's absolute path. Absent for built-ins.

summary.description: One line: what the command does. Always present for a built-in.

usage.description: A built-in's usage lists its subcommands separated by ' | '.

input.description: The data the command takes. Absent: a built-in takes none; a plugin didn't say.

output.description: The data the command gives. Absent: a built-in gives none; a plugin didn't say.

roles.description: What the command is. Absent: a built-in holds none; a plugin didn't say.

shadowed.description: True for a plugin that a built-in of the same name hides: rpt <name> never runs it.

description.description: What a command prints for --describe: one JSON object on one line, then exit 0. Every plugin and every built-in answers it.

summary.description: One line: what the command does.

usage.description: One line, e.g. rpt parse-nuclei < results.jsonl.

input.description: The data the command takes. Absent: not said.

output.description: The data the command gives. Absent: not said.

roles.description: What the command is. Absent: not said.

The roles a command holds, each a promise: checker emits problem records about the report, exits 1 only when one is an error, and never changes the report; filter reads records on stdin and writes records on stdout; writer changes the report, only through $RPT_BIN write commands; renderer reads a report record and writes a document to a place it is given (a file or folder flag), never changes the report and writes no records to stdout.

dataType.description: records for an rpt JSON Lines stream; otherwise <format> or <format>/<tool>, lowercase, chosen by the plugin author, e.g. xml/nessus, jsonl/nuclei, pdf.
